title: Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression by IRLS and EM
text: Count outcomes, number articles student publishes number times person visits doctor, usually modelled Poisson regression. Poisson model forces variance equal mean, real count data often overdispersed (variance much larger mean) often contain zeros Poisson model predicts. Ignoring either feature gives standard errors small misleading conclusions. negative binomial (NB) regression model handles overdispersion adding dispersion parameter θ\theta, zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model additionally allows zeros come separate “structural zero” process. available R MASS::glm.nb() pscl::zeroinfl(). goal project implement models scratch R package, nbzinbSiam, using iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS), Newton–Raphson EM algorithm, without calling optim() general-purpose optimizer. show package reproduces reference implementations, check simulation recovers known parameters, use analyse physician visits NMES1988 data.

title: Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression by IRLS and EM
text: NMES1988 data (Deb Trivedi 1997), included AER package, record number physician office visits (visits) 1987–88 4,406 people aged 66 US National Medical Expenditure Survey. model visits covariates hospital: number hospital stays; health: self-perceived health, levels poor, average (reference level) excellent; chronic: number chronic conditions; gender: female (reference) male; school: number years education; insurance: whether person private insurance (reference). mean number visits 5.77, variance 45.69, 8 times mean. Poisson distribution variance equal mean, data strongly overdispersed. addition, 683 people (15.5%) made visit , Poisson distribution mean predicts 0.3% zeros (14 people). Figure 1 shows features: far many zeros much longer right tail Poisson distribution allows. motivate NB ZINB models. Figure 1: Observed frequencies physician office visits (bars) frequencies expected Poisson distribution mean (points). last bar collects 30 visits. fit three models count-model covariates listed : Poisson regression (glm(), reference), NB regression nbreg(), ZINB regression zinbreg(). Following project description, zero-inflation part ZINB model uses hospital, chronic, gender, school insurance. also tried adding health zero part: raises log-likelihood 0.08 two extra parameters, neither health coefficient significant, AIC (24215.3 vs 24211.4) BIC (24323.9 vs 24307.3) prefer smaller zero model, keep . Table 4: Model comparison NMES1988 (observed zeros = 683). Table 4 compares three models. Poisson model fits poorly: predicts 47 zeros 683 observed, AIC 11,600 higher NB model’s. Allowing overdispersion (θ̂=\hat\theta = 1.21) fixes problem, NB model still -predicts zeros (608 expected vs 683 observed). ZINB model predicts 709 zeros, closer observed count, improves log-likelihood 79.8 cost 6 extra parameters. Unlike bioChemists example, AIC BIC favour ZINB model (AIC 24211.4 vs 24359.1; BIC 24307.3 vs 24416.6). Table 5: Count part: incidence rate ratios (IRR) 95% Wald confidence intervals. Table 6: ZINB zero part: odds ratios () structural zero (person visit physician circumstances), 95% Wald confidence intervals. Dispersion. NB model estimates θ̂=\hat\theta = 1.21 (SE 0.034). person whose expected number visits equals sample mean 5.77, NB variance μ+μ2/θ\mu + \mu^2/\theta 33.4, almost six times Poisson variance. (observed variance 45.7 larger still, also includes variation expected visits people.) Count part (Table 5). Holding variables fixed, using ZINB count model, describes people visit physicians: additional chronic condition multiplies expected number visits 1.14 (14% ), hospital stay 1.22. People poor health make 33% visits average health, people excellent health 27% fewer. Private insurance raises expected number visits 13%, year schooling 2.2%, men make 8% fewer visits women. effects significant 1% level models, signs. ZINB count effects somewhat smaller NB effects (example, insurance: IRR 1.25 NB model vs 1.13 ZINB count model), ZINB model part covariate’s effect works zero part instead. Zero part (Table 6). odds ratios describe belongs group visit physician : additional chronic condition multiplies odds structural zero 0.29, 71% reduction: people chronic conditions almost always see doctor. Private insurance multiplies odds 0.31 (69% lower), year schooling 0.92. Men 1.91 times odds women structural non-users. effect hospital stays large size (0.45) marginally significant (p = 0.057). estimate imprecise people hospital stay made physician visit (65 865), data carry little information structural zeros group. Several covariates therefore act parts direction: chronic conditions, insurance education make person less likely avoid physicians entirely lead visits among see one, men likely non-users make fewer visits. prefer ZINB model data. clearly best AIC BIC, reproduces number zeros much better NB model, two parts sensible interpretation: “never-user” process driven mainly chronic illness, insurance, education gender, count process often users see physician. NB model remains reasonable, simpler summary count effects, since incidence rate ratios signs similar sizes.
